question: How can the two powers appear distinct if the supreme and bliss are undivided?
premises: The two powers share the same nature and do not exist otherwise.
The supreme and bliss are by their own nature free from division.
inference: The apparent duality of the powers does not contradict the undivided nature of the supreme and bliss.
uncertainties: The verse poses an objection that is answered in the next verse.
plain_english: Those very two powers share that same nature and do not stand apart; yet the supreme and bliss are, by their own nature, free from division.
